title: Four-day dumbbell training
description: Four fixed home sessions with structured warm-up, workout and cooldown activities. Loads are selected and changed by the user; no staged progression blocks.
assumptions: Dumbbells, a stable flat bench or seat, floor space and a wall or fixed support.
No adjustable bench, barbell, squat rack, cable machine or step platform is required.
Use only comfortable controlled movements and loads that can be positioned safely.

exercises.name: Dumbbell bench press
cues: Plant both feet and keep the bench stable.
Keep wrists stacked over forearms; lower under control.
Keep elbows roughly 30-60 degrees from the torso; use a comfortable depth.
Use only dumbbells you can position and put down safely.
exercises.regression: Use the dumbbell floor press instead; record the changed exercise ID.

exercises.name: Neutral-grip dumbbell floor press
cues: Palms face each other; keep wrists straight.
Let upper arms touch the floor softly; do not bounce.
Press smoothly; stop before repetitions become a grind.
exercises.regression: Use less load and a comfortable range of motion.

exercises.name: Incline push-up
cues: Use a fixed surface that cannot slide or tip.
Keep head, trunk and hips in one line.
Lower the chest toward the support, then push away.
Record support height or support description every session.
exercises.regression: Use a higher fixed surface or a wall. A loose chair is not a safe support.

exercises.name: Bench-supported single-arm dumbbell row
cues: Support yourself on a stable bench; keep the trunk quiet.
Row the elbow toward the hip without twisting.
Lower smoothly and use the same range on both sides.
exercises.regression: Use a lighter dumbbell; rest between sides if needed.

exercises.name: Bent-over dumbbell reverse fly
cues: Use very light weights and a stable hip hinge.
Keep elbows softly bent; open the arms without swinging.
Stop around torso level; keep the neck relaxed.
exercises.regression: Use no added weight. If the bent-over position hurts, omit and add no replacement sets.

exercises.name: Dumbbell shrug
cues: Stand tall and lift the shoulders straight up.
Pause briefly, then lower; do not roll the shoulders.
exercises.regression: Use less load and a comfortable range of motion.

exercises.name: Goblet squat
cues: Hold one secure dumbbell close to the chest.
Keep the whole foot planted and let knees track with toes.
Squat only as low as you can control comfortably.
exercises.regression: Unloaded squat to a stable bench or sit-to-stand; record the bodyweight variant.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian deadlift
cues: Keep a soft knee bend and send the hips backward.
Keep the weights close and the spine comfortable and steady.
Stop at a hamstring stretch before your lower back rounds; floor contact is unnecessary.
Stand tall without leaning backward.
exercises.regression: Rehearse unloaded hip hinges. If uncomfortable, use a bodyweight glute bridge with its own exercise ID.

exercises.name: Reverse lunge
cues: Start unloaded, with light hand support if needed.
Step back and lower smoothly through a comfortable range.
Push through the front foot to stand; keep the movement balanced.
Log left and right separately; the side is the front working leg.
exercises.regression: Use a shorter comfortable range with hand support, or substitute the goblet-squat bodyweight variant.

exercises.name: Standing calf raise on floor
cues: Use a stable support for balance.
Rise smoothly, pause, and lower slowly on the flat floor.
Begin bodyweight; later use one dumbbell and retain the same support.
exercises.regression: Use less load and a comfortable range of motion.

exercises.name: Standing dumbbell shoulder press
cues: Keep ribs over hips and knees relaxed.
Start with elbows slightly in front of the torso.
Press in a comfortable path without leaning backward.
exercises.regression: Use lighter weights. If overhead motion is painful, omit it and seek assessment rather than forcing the movement.

exercises.name: Dumbbell lateral raise
cues: Use light weights with a small elbow bend.
Raise slightly forward of your sides to about shoulder level if comfortable.
Keep thumbs neutral or slightly upward; avoid swinging.
exercises.regression: Use less load and a comfortable range of motion.

exercises.name: Standing dumbbell curl
cues: Curl both arms together; count one simultaneous repetition as one rep.
Keep the upper arms quiet and wrists comfortable.
Lower under control without leaning or swinging.
exercises.regression: Use less load and a comfortable range of motion.

exercises.name: Dumbbell hammer curl
cues: Keep palms facing each other and curl both arms together.
Count one simultaneous repetition as one rep.
Keep elbows close to the torso; do not swing.
exercises.regression: Use less load and a comfortable range of motion.

exercises.name: Dumbbell triceps extension on floor
cues: Use light dumbbells and a secure grip.
Bend at the elbows with the upper arms steady.
Keep the weights away from your face and move slowly.
exercises.regression: If elbows are uncomfortable, omit this exercise; keep only the pain-free close-grip floor press already in the plan.

exercises.name: Close-grip dumbbell floor press
cues: Use a neutral grip and keep elbows comfortably close.
Lower gently until upper arms touch the floor.
Do not bang the dumbbells together or bounce the elbows.
exercises.regression: Use less load and a comfortable range of motion.

exercises.name: Dead bug
cues: Lie on your back with hips and knees bent.
Exhale gently while moving opposite arm and leg.
Keep the trunk quiet and shorten the reach if your back arches.
Side means the extending leg.
exercises.regression: Move only the legs or tap one heel at a time.

exercises.name: Side plank
cues: Put the elbow under the shoulder.
Keep the trunk aligned and breathe normally.
Start with bent knees if necessary.
Side means the side supporting the body on the floor.
exercises.regression: Use bent knees and 10-15 second holds.

exercises.name: Glute bridge
cues: Keep feet planted and ribs relaxed.
Lift the hips by squeezing the glutes; do not arch the back.
Pause briefly, then lower smoothly.
exercises.regression: Use less load and a comfortable range of motion.

exercises.name: Easy walk
cues: Walk at a pace where you can speak in full sentences.
Use flat, safe ground; no running is required.
exercises.regression: Walk for 5-10 minutes and gradually extend the time.

exercises.name: Gentle mobility circuit
cues: Use easy shoulder circles, ankle circles and comfortable trunk rotations.
Move slowly and stay in a pain-free range.
Skip any movement that causes symptoms.
exercises.regression: Use less load and a comfortable range of motion.

exercises.name: Push-up
cues: Keep head, trunk and hips aligned.
Lower under control with elbows comfortably angled away from the body.
Stop while two or three clean repetitions remain.
exercises.regression: Select incline-pushup and use a fixed support that cannot slide; keep the new exercise identity and support height.

exercises.name: Seated dumbbell shoulder press
cues: Sit tall on a stable flat seat with feet planted.
Keep ribs over hips and do not lean backward.
Keep elbows slightly forward and use a comfortable pressing range.
exercises.regression: Use lighter dumbbells, or substitute the existing standing dumbbell press if that position is more comfortable. Omit painful overhead work.

exercises.name: Seated dumbbell rear-delt fly
cues: Sit and hinge forward with a comfortable, steady trunk.
Use light dumbbells and softly bent elbows.
Open the arms without throwing the weights or forcing the shoulders.
exercises.regression: Use less load or the existing standing reverse fly if its position is more comfortable.

exercises.name: Seated French triceps extension
cues: Hold one secure dumbbell in both hands.
Keep the torso tall and bend at the elbows without arching the back.
Move slowly and keep a secure grip; log the one dumbbell weight once.
exercises.regression: Use the existing dumbbell triceps extension on the floor if overhead positioning is uncomfortable. Do not force elbow or shoulder pain.

exercises.name: Dumbbell split squat
cues: Keep both feet on the floor in a staggered stance.
Lower straight down through a comfortable range; the front leg is the logged side.
Use a stable hand support and the bodyweight variant if balance is difficult.
exercises.regression: Select bodyweight-split-squat and use a fixed hand support; no rear-foot elevation is required.

exercises.name: Supported bodyweight split squat
cues: Use the split-squat movement with no dumbbells and light hand support.
Keep both feet on the floor and start with a shallow comfortable range.
exercises.regression: Use the bodyweight squat or a stable sit-to-stand.

exercises.name: Dumbbell glute bridge
cues: Rest one dumbbell securely across the hips with padding if needed and hold it in place.
Lift by squeezing the glutes, keeping ribs relaxed.
Do not overarch the lower back or let the dumbbell roll.
exercises.regression: Select glute-bridge and perform the same floor movement without added weight.

exercises.name: Supported single-leg dumbbell calf raise
cues: Use the flat floor and a fixed hand support for balance.
Hold one dumbbell securely in the free hand; the logged side is the working leg.
Rise, pause, then lower slowly without bouncing.
exercises.regression: Select bodyweight-single-leg-calf-raise; if needed use the existing bilateral calf-raise instead.

exercises.name: Supported single-leg calf raise
cues: Use a fixed hand support and the flat floor.
Lift and lower one heel slowly while the other foot is off the ground.
exercises.regression: Use the existing bilateral calf-raise with both feet on the floor.

exercises.name: Crunch
cues: Keep feet on the floor and lift the shoulder blades a small controlled distance.
Exhale as you curl and avoid pulling your neck.
exercises.regression: Use a smaller range or substitute dead-bug if comfortable.

exercises.name: Reverse crunch
cues: Start with bent knees and gently curl the pelvis off the floor.
Avoid swinging the legs or throwing the hips overhead.
Lower slowly; a small controlled movement is enough.
exercises.regression: Use a smaller pelvic curl or substitute dead-bug.

exercises.name: Alternating heel touches
cues: Keep knees bent and feet planted, reaching gently toward each heel.
Count every heel touch as one repetition, alternating sides.
Thirty total touches means fifteen per side; keep the reach controlled.
exercises.regression: Keep the head supported between repetitions or use shorter, comfortable reaches.

exercises.name: Plank shoulder taps
cues: Use a wide enough foot position to keep the pelvis steady.
Tap the opposite shoulder without rocking the trunk.
Count every tap as one repetition, alternating sides.
exercises.regression: Perform from the knees or use a fixed high support. Stop if the wrists or shoulders hurt.

exercises.name: March on the spot
cues: March comfortably and gradually increase the pace.
Keep breathing easy; no high knees or jumping are required.
exercises.regression: Use a gentle seated march or a slower pace.

exercises.name: Arm circles
cues: Make small comfortable circles and gradually enlarge them.
Change direction halfway; keep shoulders relaxed.
exercises.regression: Use smaller circles or one arm at a time.

exercises.name: Standing trunk rotations
cues: Turn gently from side to side without forcing end range.
Count each turn to one side as one repetition.
Keep knees soft; do not combine a deep toe touch with a fast twist.
exercises.regression: Use a smaller range and slower movement.

exercises.name: Shoulder-blade squeeze
cues: Draw the shoulder blades gently together.
Keep the neck relaxed and avoid shrugging.
exercises.regression: Use a smaller squeeze without added resistance.

exercises.name: Unloaded hip hinge
cues: Soften the knees and send the hips back.
Keep the trunk steady and return to standing without leaning backward.
exercises.regression: Use a small range and light support on a stable surface.

exercises.name: Bodyweight squat
cues: Keep the feet planted and knees tracking with the toes.
Lower through a comfortable range and stand smoothly.
exercises.regression: Sit to a stable bench and stand, using support if needed.

exercises.name: Lateral lunge warm-up
cues: Shift gently onto one leg while keeping the other more extended.
Use a small range and keep the planted foot steady.
Perform the target on each side without bouncing.
exercises.regression: Use a shallower side-to-side weight shift with hand support.

exercises.name: Half-kneeling hamstring rocks
cues: Pad the kneeling knee and extend the front leg comfortably.
Rock the hips back gently until a mild stretch, then release.
Do not force a toe touch or lock the knee hard.
exercises.regression: Use a standing supported hamstring hinge if kneeling is uncomfortable.

exercises.name: Cat and camel
cues: Move the back gently between a comfortable arch and rounding.
One full movement through both positions counts as one repetition.
Use easy motion without forcing either end range.
exercises.regression: Use a smaller range or a comfortable standing trunk movement.

exercises.name: Cross-body shoulder stretch
cues: Bring one arm across the chest with gentle support.
Keep the shoulder down; stretch mildly without pain.
exercises.regression: Reduce the pull or omit if the shoulder is uncomfortable.

exercises.name: Overhead triceps stretch
cues: Bend one elbow overhead and use only gentle guidance.
Keep ribs down and breathe normally; do not force the elbow back.
exercises.regression: Lower the arm or omit if overhead motion is uncomfortable.

exercises.name: Doorway chest stretch
cues: Place one forearm on a stable doorway or wall and turn away slightly.
Use a mild chest stretch without shoulder pain.
Work one side at a time and avoid forcing the shoulder back.
exercises.regression: Use a lower arm position and a smaller turn, or omit.

exercises.name: Supported quadriceps stretch
cues: Hold a stable support and bring one heel gently toward the buttock.
Keep knees comfortable and avoid arching the back.
exercises.regression: Use a smaller bend or omit if reaching the foot is difficult or painful.

exercises.name: Wall calf stretch
cues: Step one leg back with its heel down.
Lean toward the wall until a mild calf stretch; do not bounce.
exercises.regression: Use a shorter stance and less lean.

exercises.name: Half-kneeling hip-flexor stretch
cues: Pad the back knee and gently tuck the pelvis.
Move only a little forward without arching the lower back.
exercises.regression: Use a supported standing staggered stance if kneeling is uncomfortable.

exercises.name: Child pose stretch
cues: Sit the hips toward the heels only as far as comfortable.
Reach forward gently and breathe normally without forcing the knees.
exercises.regression: Place hands on a stable support and hinge gently from standing, or omit.

No high-speed Russian twists or declined bench work are required.

programs.name: Four fixed dumbbell sessions

phases.name: Regular training
phases.notes: Repeat the same sessions. Choose current loads manually. There are no scheduled changes to sets, volume or exercises.

programs.transitionPolicy: No staged progression or automatic phase transition. The single phase only preserves compatibility with the existing program engine.
programs.missedDayPolicy: Resume when recovered and do not combine missed workouts. Keep at least one easier day between the two upper-body sessions.
